title: Dedicated capacity admission-control policy and SLA expectations notebook
creator: Ethan Morales
description: Objective: Define an admission-control (intake + gating) policy for enterprise dedicated capacity requests that translates customer workload signals into SLA expectations, reserved throughput commitments, GPU class recommendations, scaling policies, and a clear fallback ladder. Deliverables: intake rubric, GPU->SLA mapping table, tiered scaling & burst policy, canary/onboarding checklist, and an engineering hand-off with acceptance criteria. Scope excludes pricing/legal negotiation templates which remain with sales and legal.
acceptance_criteria: New intake form captures peak RPS, p50/p95 latency targets, request pattern (steady vs bursty), and model characteristics (sequence length, KV cache sensitivity)
A mapping table showing recommended GPU families, expected token/sec, and estimated cost-per-1M-tokens for three workload archetypes
SLA bands (gold/silver/bronze) defined with clear operational guarantees and documented fallback behavior
Autoscale / burst policy proposals with preconditions, cooldowns, and preemption rules documented
Stakeholder sign-off from Eng (runtime), Sales, and Solutions Engineering and a TODO hand-off ticket to ENG for implementation
comments: 2026-03-10 Ethan Morales: Kickoff—aligned with Solutions Eng on required intake fields. Agreed to prototype mapping using telemetry from three reference customers.

2026-03-11 Lena Cho: Added preliminary GPU class mapping draft (A100-80GB for high-throughput; A10G for mid; T4 for low-cost). Noted trade-offs: latency variance on quantized models and KV cache miss penalties.

2026-03-12 Runtime eng review (Samir Patel): Recommended adding sequence-length distribution and KV cache sensitivity as required signals; warned that token/sec estimates need safety margin of 20% for peak concurrency.
2026-03-12 Solutions Eng feedback (Priya Singh): Customers commonly measure qps differently; added guidance on normalizing RPS to model tokens/sec and provided two customer anonymized examples.

2026-03-13 PM review: Incorporated feedback and created proposed SLA bands. Action: review with Legal for contractual language and with Security for KMS/HSM requirements when private deployments are requested.
next_steps: Iterate GPU->SLA mapping with runtime perf team using reference traces (owner: Lena Cho, due 2026-03-20)
Run tabletop with Solutions Eng + Sales to validate questionnaire signal alignment (owner: Ethan Morales, due 2026-03-18)
Open engineering implementation epic that codifies admission-control checks and returns structured recommendation payloads to Sales UI (owner: ENG PM, due 2026-03-25)
Legal & Security review for SLA language and private deployment KMS requirements (owners: Legal, Security; requested completion 2026-03-22)
Publish intake rubric + onboarding checklist to Console docs and internal playbooks (owner: DEX, due 2026-03-29)
resolution_plan: Phase 1: Finalize intake questionnaire and GPU mapping table; ship internal playbook for Sales and Solutions Eng
Phase 2: Implement runtime admission checks and recommendation API; include 20% safety buffer and fallback model variants
Phase 3: Pilot with 2 enterprise customers, collect telemetry, and refine throughput estimates; prepare SLA contract language
Phase 4: General rollout and include in Dedicated onboarding flow in Console
